//: The brick kiln's firebox. The same arrangement as the mud one with the shell course laid in fired brick instead of mud brick, one colour to a firebox so it can match the kiln it is set into. The mouth lining - the top row, and the part the flame actually touches - is fire clay whatever colour the face is, as the wicket is; the 5x5 drum around them will take any fired brick.

A draft vent in fired brick, to cap a brick kiln in the same colour as its shell. It works exactly as the mud one does; mortared like the brick blocks it sits among, which also keeps it from being the bottom two rows of the firebox recipe.

The wicket, two panels to a craft because the entrance is one block wide and two tall. Vanilla's own kiln door recipe with the metal list moved down a tier: the strapping and the pintles are on the outer face, where a thick brick panel keeps them a long way under the copper's melting point, so there is no reason this needs iron. Bronze is accepted on the same argument - tin bronze melts cooler than copper does, and neither is anywhere near the fire.
name: Kiln wicket panel
